sections.heading: Lead
Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
On 12 September 2016, the song was at number 30 on ''[[The Official Chart#The Official Chart Update|The Official Chart Update]]'' in the [[United Kingdom]].<ref>[http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/lady-gagas-perfect-illusion-set-to-be-this-weeks-highest-new-entry-on-the-official-uk-singles-chart__16295/ Lady Gaga's Perfect Illusion set to be this week's highest new entry on the Official UK Singles Chart]. [[Official Charts Company]].</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://metro.co.uk/2016/10/16/is-james-arthur-facing-a-copyright-lawsuit-over-say-you-wont-let-go-6194923/|title=Is James Arthur facing a copyright lawsuit over Say You Won't Let Go?|last=Starkey|first=Adam|date=16 October 2016|work=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]|publisher=[[DMG Media]]|access-date=16 August 2017}}</ref> On 16 September 2016, the song entered the [[UK Singles Chart]] at number 25, and peaked at number one two weeks later, becoming Arthur's second number one and spending three consecutive weeks at the top.  The song was ranked the nineteenth biggest-selling song of 2016 in the UK, making Arthur the biggest-selling British male artist of the year.<ref name="UK year-end"/> By the second week of January 2017, it had surpassed the one million sales mark, making him the first-ever ''X Factor'' act to have two singles sell over a million copies in his homeland.<ref>[http://www.buzzjack.com/forums/index.php?showtopic=197077 YTD T40 Singles/Albums (with estimated sales), Week 2 : 19/1/17]. BuzzJack Music Forum</ref>

In the United States, the song debuted at #100 on the date November 12, 2016. The song peaked at #11 for two non-consecutive weeks being kept out of the top 10 from "[[Malibu (Miley Cyrus song)|Malibu]]" by [[Miley Cyrus]] the first week and "[[Congratulations (Post Malone song)|Congratulations]]" by [[Post Malone]] the second week. It spent 52 weeks on the chart.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://musicchartsarchive.com/singles-chart/2017-06-03|title=Singles Chart for 2017-06-03|website=Music Charts Archive|language=en|access-date=2020-01-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://musicchartsarchive.com/singles-chart/2017-06-24|title=Singles Chart for 2017-06-24|website=Music Charts Archive|language=en|access-date=2020-01-31}}</ref> The song is his first single to chart on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], making Arthur only the third winner to chart on the Hot 100 following [[Leona Lewis]] and [[Little Mix]]. In May 2017, the song reached No. 1 on the Adult Pop Songs Airplay Chart, more than six months after its release in the US.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/james-arthur-say-you-wont-let-go-adult-pop-songs-airplay/|title=James Arthur's 'Say You Won't Let Go' Tops Adult Pop Songs Airplay Chart|date=May 22, 2017 |author= Gary Trust|magazine=Billboard }}</ref> The song was certified diamond in the US by the RIAA on February 15, 2023.<ref>{{cite certification|region=United States|artist=James Arthur|access-date=February 15, 2023}}</ref> The song has sold over 1,208,000 digital copies in the US as of September 2017.<ref name="ussales">{{cite news|url=http://www.defjampromo.com/files/2009/10/BB-Digital-Songs-Chart-Wk.-Ending-9-28-17.pdf|title=Nielsen SoundScan charts – Digital Songs – Week Ending: 09/28/2017|publisher=[[Nielsen SoundScan]]|access-date=October 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171002211120/http://www.defjampromo.com/files/2009/10/BB-Digital-Songs-Chart-Wk.-Ending-9-28-17.pdf|archive-date=October 2, 2017}}</ref> It was the eighth best-selling song of 2017 in the US, with 1,195,000 copies sold in 2017.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/ed-sheeran-divide-nielsen-music-top-album-2017/|title=Ed Sheeran's 'Divide' Is Nielsen Music's Top Album of 2017 in U.S.|author=Keith Caulfield|magazine=Billboard|date=3 January 2018|access-date=4 January 2018}}</ref>

By 2021, the single had sold 2,676,756 copies in the UK.<ref>[https://www.musicweek.com/talent/read/james-arthur-on-new-music-respect-and-making-bangers/082616 James Arthur on new music, respect and making bangers | Talent | Music Week<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

On 15 September 2016, the song entered the [[Irish Singles Chart]] at number 91 before peaking at number one on 14 October and spending four non-consecutive weeks at the top of the charts. The song has also charted in [[Australia]], [[France]], [[New Zealand]] and [[Sweden]]. On February 26, 2017, it was announced on Channel 4's ''[[Sunday Brunch]]'' that the single had sold 2 million copies worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/SundayBrunchC4/status/835813188792901632|title=Sunday Brunch on Twitter|website=[[Twitter]]|date=26 February 2017|access-date=26 February 2017}}</ref>

As of October 2024, the song is the 15th most streamed song in [[Spotify]] history, having [[List of Spotify streaming records#Most-streamed songs|amassed over three billion streams on the platform]].
sections.text:
On 12 September 2016, the song was at number 30 on The Official Chart Update in the United Kingdom. On 16 September 2016, the song entered the UK Singles Chart at number 25, and peaked at number one two weeks later, becoming Arthur's second number one and spending three consecutive weeks at the top.  The song was ranked the nineteenth biggest-selling song of 2016 in the UK, making Arthur the biggest-selling British male artist of the year. By the second week of January 2017, it had surpassed the one million sales mark, making him the first-ever X Factor act to have two singles sell over a million copies in his homeland.

In the United States, the song debuted at #100 on the date November 12, 2016. The song peaked at #11 for two non-consecutive weeks being kept out of the top 10 from "Malibu" by Miley Cyrus the first week and "Congratulations" by Post Malone the second week. It spent 52 weeks on the chart. The song is his first single to chart on the US Billboard Hot 100, making Arthur only the third winner to chart on the Hot 100 following Leona Lewis and Little Mix. In May 2017, the song reached No. 1 on the Adult Pop Songs Airplay Chart, more than six months after its release in the US. The song was certified diamond in the US by the RIAA on February 15, 2023. The song has sold over 1,208,000 digital copies in the US as of September 2017. It was the eighth best-selling song of 2017 in the US, with 1,195,000 copies sold in 2017.

By 2021, the single had sold 2,676,756 copies in the UK.

On 15 September 2016, the song entered the Irish Singles Chart at number 91 before peaking at number one on 14 October and spending four non-consecutive weeks at the top of the charts. The song has also charted in Australia, France, New Zealand and Sweden. On February 26, 2017, it was announced on Channel 4's Sunday Brunch that the single had sold 2 million copies worldwide.

As of October 2024, the song is the 15th most streamed song in Spotify history, having amassed over three billion streams on the platform.
